    ]
  },
  "n_columns": 5,
  "n_justification": "The 500-2400 m range (1900 m relief) is divided into five ~380 m elevation bands to resolve the rain-snow transition and snowpack gradient that dominate Yakima hydrology. Five columns capture (1) low-elevation rain-dominated valley, (2) transitional rain-snow, (3) seasonal snow zone near SNOTEL sensors, (4) reliable snow zone, and (5) high alpine. This is enough to resolve the phase-transition physics without over-fitting to limited driver contrasts (elevation + soil only).",

parsed.n_justification: The 500-2400 m range (1900 m relief) is divided into five ~380 m elevation bands to resolve the rain-snow transition and snowpack gradient that dominate Yakima hydrology. Five columns capture (1) low-elevation rain-dominated valley, (2) transitional rain-snow, (3) seasonal snow zone near SNOTEL sensors, (4) reliable snow zone, and (5) high alpine. This is enough to resolve the phase-transition physics without over-fitting to limited driver contrasts (elevation + soil only).
assumptions: Single-column runs are surrogate points for elevation bands; no lateral routing between columns
Column lats/lons chosen along the basin's elevation gradient near SNOTEL sites for validation of SWE
Soil textures assigned per band from typical Cascade montane profiles; can be overridden by SSURGO/gridded surface data
GSWP3/CLMNCEP forcing used with elevation-based downscaling of temperature and precipitation phase
STOP_N in years covering full 1980-2018 forcing after a spin-up cycle to equilibrate soil/snow states
Monthly (default) history output; switch to daily if finer melt-timing analysis is needed
